subject: Hosted eval: quickstart endpoints, rate bands & burst capacity
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@finscale.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Mar 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted eval: quickstart endpoints, rate bands & burst capacity

Hi Alicia — great meeting today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we don’t lose momentum: 

1) Your goal: prototype a hosted integration to power a conversational assistant for our underwriting UI, expected peak traffic ~2.5k requests/day initially, target latency <300ms for single-turn prompts, and ability to stream partial responses for chat.
2) Deployment preference: you signaled preference to start on Hosted API for speed (no infra lift), but FinScale security wants clarity on burst handling, VPC egress options, and SOC2 artifacts before sign-off.
3) Quickstart items I can share today (attached): a short curl example to hit a sandbox endpoint, a one-pager on hosted rate bands, and an onboarding checklist that outlines keys, roles, and expected test traffic.

Questions / asks from our side:
- Can you confirm which teams need access to sandbox keys (AI engineering, security auditors)?
- Do you anticipate sustained throughput >10k reqs/day within 30 days (this helps us advise Hosted vs Dedicated)?

Next steps I recommend: we provision a sandbox key scoped to your test namespace and give you a two-week hosted slice (burst-friendly) so your engineers can validate latency and streaming. If you prefer, we can run a short load profile together to observe behavior and KV/cache effectiveness.

I’ve attached hosted-ratebands.pdf that summarizes default limits and burst handling. High-level: default per-key baseline is 200 requests/min with token-based floors; we support queued bursts up to 5x baseline for short windows. For predictable heavy workloads (sustained >5M tokens/day), we recommend Dedicated pools; Private VPC is an onboarding path if you require customer-managed networking.

If it helps, Ben can jump on a 30-minute ops call next week to walk the team through the sandbox run and rate-slicing.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198
Redwood Inference

From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@finscale.com>

Date: Sat, 11 Mar 2028 10:02:14 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted eval: quickstart endpoints, rate bands & burst capacity

Thanks Priya — helpful summary. A few quick clarifications from my side after sharing with our security and infra leads: 

- Bursts: when you say queued bursts up to 5x baseline, can you clarify max sustained burst window and how queueing impacts tail latency (for streaming clients)? We may need 30–60s bursts during batch scoring windows.
- VPC / egress: our security team prefers that traffic to hosted endpoints is routed over our VPC egress IPs (to allow egress filtering). Is there a simple way for Hosted API to restrict access to specific customer egress IPs?
- SOC2 + keys: can you share SOC2 report and the sandbox key link (we’ll hand to our auditors)? Also want any guidance on key rotation cadence.

Small ask: could you send the curl example and a small sample that demonstrates streaming responses (we prototype in JS and Python)?

We’re leaning toward Hosted for speed, but if any of the constraints above are blockers, we’ll revisit Dedicated. We expect to go to a pilot (not prod) in 2–3 weeks if security signs off.

—Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Head of AI, FinScale
alicia.gomez@finscale.com

Hi Alicia — thanks for the follow-up and the clear questions. Answers below and I’ve attached the curl snippet and the ratebands PDF for quick reference.

Bursts & queueing: our hosted runtime uses a short FIFO admission queue for spikes. Baseline per-key request ceiling is 200 reqs/min (configurable per account). For short windows we can allow bursts up to ~1000 reqs/min for up to 30–60s before admission starts to throttle; streaming connections are prioritized through a fast-path so partial tokens are delivered to clients quickly. Tail latency during burst phases increases modestly (we typically see p95 increase by ~50–120ms depending on sequence length).

VPC egress / IP allowlist: Hosted API cannot be deployed inside your VPC, but we support IP allowlisting at the API-key level so you can constrain which customer egress ranges may call your sandbox keys. If you need full VPC-private routing, that’s the Private deployment path — we can discuss timelines and onboarding steps.

SOC2 + keys: attaching SOC2 summary and our compliance contact in the attachment bundle; sandbox key link below is a single-use test key we provisioned for FinScale: https://app.redwood.com/sandbox/keys/FS-0784. Key rotation: recommended 30–90 days for sandbox; for production we recommend automated rotation with our KMS integration (we document setup in the onboarding checklist).

Quickstart & streaming samples: see attached redwood_quickstart_curl.txt (curl + JS streaming snippet) — the JS sample demonstrates how to pipe partial responses to your UI using EventSource-style streaming.

When to consider Dedicated: if you expect sustained >5M tokens/day or need dedicated GPU pools and stronger SLA terms on throughput, we advise Dedicated. For your stated pilot traffic (~2.5k reqs/day), Hosted with an initial slice should be the fastest path. If you want, Ben can run a 30-minute technical session with your infra team to walk IP allowlisting, sandbox provisioning, and a short load run to observe tail behavior.

Proposed next steps:
- I’ll provision access to the sandbox key for the AI engineering and security email aliases you shared (please confirm: ai-team@finscale.com, security@finscale.com).
- Book a 30-minute ops run with Ben — are you available Wed 14 Mar 10:00–10:30 PT or Thu 15 Mar 9:00–9:30 PT?

If you confirm the emails to grant access to, I’ll send the sandbox invite and put Ben on the calendar.

Best,
